summary: Add ForeignKey constraint on account_user.referrer_id by first nullifying orphan references, adding the constraint as NOT VALID to permit concurrent version writes, deploying the new version with state_only, retiring the old version, and finally validating the FK constraint to enforce referential integrity.
write_consistency: During the overlap between deploy_new and retire_old, the old version continues writing referrer_id as integer; the new version writes referrer_id via its FK-aware code. The FK constraint is added as NOT VALID, which prevents immediate enforcement on new writes, allowing the old version to keep inserting values without constraint violations. After retire_old, the FK is validated to ensure data integrity. The note column remains untouched as it is separate from referrer_id.

stages.description: Set referrer_id to NULL for rows referencing non-existent account_user IDs, ensuring no existing data violates the upcoming FK constraint.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);

stages.description: Add ForeignKey constraint on referrer_id referencing account_user.id as NOT VALID, so it does not block old version writes during concurrent traffic.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT referrer_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id) NOT VALID;

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; old version no longer serves traffic.\n
Validate the FK constraint to enforce referential integrity after the old version has been retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user VALIDATE CONSTRAINT referrer_id_fk;
